title: kith-tui client.rs: unit tests with wiremock
description:
What: Write unit tests for client.rs using wiremock to mock kithds HTTP endpoints.

Oracle: test vectors are constructed manually from the wire protocol spec. No value is derived from running the code under test.

Tests to implement (all in kith-tui/src/client.rs #[cfg(test)] or a separate tests/ file):

1. test: fetch_session_happy_path
   Oracle: hand-craft a JSON response matching the ClientSession struct.
   Setup: wiremock::MockServer::start().await; mount a GET /.well-known/jmap mock that returns:
   {"primaryAccounts":{"urn:kith:chat:1":"a-self"},"apiUrl":"https://PLACEHOLDER/jmap/api","eventSourceUrl":"https://PLACEHOLDER/jmap/events","state":"s-1"}
   where PLACEHOLDER is the mock server URI.
   Action: call fetch_session(&client, &mock_server.uri()).await
   Assert: result is Ok, account_id() == Some("a-self"), state == "s-1"

2. test: fetch_session_404_returns_error
   Oracle: HTTP 404 must produce ClientError::Http (reqwest surfaces HTTP status errors via error_for_status).
   Setup: mount a GET /.well-known/jmap mock that returns 404 with empty body.
   Action: call fetch_session(&client, &mock_server.uri()).await
   Assert: result is Err(ClientError::Http(_))

3. test: call_jmap_round_trip
   Oracle: hand-craft a JmapRequest and a JmapResponse.
   JmapRequest: { using: ["urn:ietf:params:jmap:core","urn:kith:chat:1"], methodCalls: [["Chat/get",{"accountId":"a-self"},"c0"]] }
   JmapResponse: { methodResponses: [["Chat/get",{"accountId":"a-self","list":[],"state":"s-2"},"c0"]], sessionState: "s-1" }
   Setup: mount POST /jmap/api mock that returns 200 with the JmapResponse JSON above.
   Action: build a JmapRequest as above; call call_jmap(&client, &(mock_server.uri() + "/jmap/api"), &req).await
   Assert: result is Ok; method_responses[0].0 == "Chat/get"; session_state == "s-1"

4. test: parse_sse_single_event
   Oracle: RFC 8895 SSE format + kithd events.rs comment (line 102):
   {"changed":{"a-self":{"Message":"s-42"}}}
   This is an inline test of the SSE parser logic — no mock server needed.
   Extract the SSE parser into a helper function (parse_sse_event(block: &str) -> Vec<StateChange>)
   that can be unit-tested without spawning an HTTP connection.
   Input: "event: state\ndata: {\"changed\":{\"a-self\":{\"Message\":\"s-42\"}}}"
   Assert: returns vec with one StateChange { type_name: "Message", new_state: "s-42" }

5. test: parse_sse_ping_event_is_ignored
   Oracle: kithd sends ping events; they carry no StateChange data.
   Input: "event: ping\ndata: {\"interval\":30}"
   Assert: parse_sse_event returns empty vec

6. test: parse_sse_multiple_types_in_one_event
   Oracle: kithd may coalesce multiple type changes into one SSE frame.
   Input: "event: state\ndata: {\"changed\":{\"a-self\":{\"Message\":\"s-43\",\"Chat\":\"s-2\"}}}"
   Assert: returns vec with exactly 2 StateChange entries (one for Message, one for Chat);
   order may differ; verify both entries present via sort or HashSet comparison.

Defensive programming rules:
- Each test must use a fresh MockServer instance (or fresh parse inputs) to avoid state leak.
- Never derive expected values from the code under test — all expected values are in the test itself.
- Tests that use wiremock::MockServer must be async (#[tokio::test]).
- SSE parse tests are synchronous (no async needed if the parser is extracted to a pure fn).
- build_client() in tests: for wiremock (plain HTTP, not HTTPS), use a plain reqwest::Client::new() or reqwest::ClientBuilder::new().danger_accept_invalid_certs(true).build().unwrap() since wiremock does not use TLS.
- Do not call unwrap() outside of test helpers; use .expect("reason") so test failures are descriptive.
